base_tool_cache_barrier_test.method: threading.Barrier(2) placed inside the stubbed upstream call, AFTER the cache-miss check (_get_from_cache returns None for both threads) and BEFORE either thread's result is written to cache (_save_to_cache) - forces the exact simultaneous-miss window the unlocked check-then-act pattern is vulnerable to, rather than hoping real timing reproduces it.
base_tool_cache_barrier_test.explanation: Both racing threads independently executed the real upstream call and both obtained the identical correct data; the plain-dict cache write (self.cache[cache_key] = (timestamp, data)) is a single atomic dict-item assignment under the GIL, so there is no possibility of a torn/partial write - whichever thread writes last simply overwrites the identical-shape tuple the other thread would have written. This is wasted redundant work under concurrent identical-key requests (a 'thundering herd' effect), not a data-integrity defect. Per the governing directive's explicit instruction, this race is audited, NOT fixed, in this pass.
